title: Categorical homotopy equivalences of Segal spaces preserve mapping spaces
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, homotopy fibers and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and the Reedy model structure of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A simplicial space is a functor $V:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$. It is a Segal space if it is Reedy fibrant and its consecutive-edge maps $V_n\to V_1\times_{V_0}\cdots\times_{V_0}V_1$ are weak homotopy equivalences for every $n\geq2$. For vertices $x,y$ of $V_0$, let $M_V(x,y)$ be the strict fiber of $(d_1,d_0):V_1\to V_0^2$. The homotopy category $hV$ has those vertices as objects, morphisms $\pi_0M_V(x,y)$, identity from $s_0$, and composition from the degree-two Segal map and $d_1$. Let $V_{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq V_1$ be the union of components representing isomorphisms in $hV$.

For $n\geq0$ let $F(n)_k=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([k],[n])$, discrete in the inner direction. Let $I[1]$ be the groupoid on objects $0,1$ with exactly one morphism between each ordered pair, and let $E$ be its ordinary nerve, regarded as a simplicial space discrete in the inner direction. Let $e_0,e_1:F(0)\to E$ select the two objects, and let $a:F(1)\to E$ select the arrow $0\to1$. For maps $f_0,f_1:A\to B$ of simplicial spaces, a categorical homotopy means a map $H:A\times E\to B$ restricting to $f_0,f_1$ at $e_0,e_1$. Let $U,V$ be Segal spaces and let $f:U\to V$ and $g:V\to U$ be maps. If $gf$ and $1_U$ are categorically homotopic and $fg$ and $1_V$ are categorically homotopic, then
$$M_U(x,y)\longrightarrow M_V(fx,fy)$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence for all vertices $x,y\in U_0$, and $hf:hU\to hV$ is an equivalence of ordinary categories. In particular every object of $hV$ is isomorphic to some $f(x)$.
